correctness.rationale: For n>=2, the 1x2xn hexagonal honeycomb perfect matchings P_{u,v} have explicit edge incidence rules. With x=d00, y=d2n and D={d1j:1<=j<=n-1}, every codimension-one subset of F={x,y}∪D extends to a perfect matching, but F cannot, so K_n[F] is boundary of an n-simplex. The ordered x-toggle then y-toggle acyclic matching of the full face poset has sole unmatched face F minus {x}. Every matching pair either lies wholly in that induced boundary or wholly outside, because toggled edges both belong to F; all outside faces match and the relative Morse deletion gives an actual elementary collapse K_n searrow K_n[F]. The half-turn maps P_{u,v} to P_{n-v,n-u}, swaps x,y and reverses n-1 D indices, so the sign on top integral H_{n-1} is (-1)^{1+floor((n-1)/2)}. Rational quotient homology follows after barycentric subdivision by exactness of finite-group invariants. Independent n=2,3 face enumeration reconstructed the missing simplex, all matches and half-turn preservation; the proof, rather than finite counts, establishes the all-n assertion.
residual_risks: Finite tests provide corroboration only; the claimed uniform or asymptotic theorem relies on the inspected analytical proof.
